---
title: SCIM provisioning
description: Keep your organization's membership in sync from your IdP with the SCIM 2.0 User resource.
---

[SSO](/docs/security/sso) authenticates whoever your IdP sends; **SCIM 2.0**
keeps the membership list in sync automatically — new hires get access,
departures lose it — without an admin inviting anyone by hand. Helio implements
the SCIM 2.0 **User** resource.

## Connect your IdP

1. In Helio, open **Settings → SCIM provisioning** (owner/admin) and select
   **Generate token**. Copy the bearer token — it is shown only once.
2. In your IdP's provisioning settings, set:
   - **SCIM base URL:** `https://<your-helio-host>/scim/v2`
   - **Authentication:** OAuth Bearer Token → paste the token from step 1.
3. Enable provisioning. Okta or Entra will probe `/ServiceProviderConfig`, then
   create, look up, and deactivate users as your directory changes.

## How users map

- **Create** (`POST /Users`) adds the person to your organization as a `viewer`
  (elevate under **Settings → Members**). It's idempotent per email.
- **Deactivate** (`PATCH active:false`) and **Delete** (`DELETE`) both remove the
  organization membership. The person's underlying account — which may belong to
  other organizations — is left intact. Deprovisioning is the security goal, so
  there is no lingering "inactive" state.
- Provisioning and deprovisioning are written to the [audit log](/docs/concepts/tenancy#auditing).

## Security model

- Every `/scim/v2` request is authenticated by the org's bearer token; an IdP
  only ever sees its own organization. Regenerating the token immediately
  invalidates the previous one.
- Only the token's **SHA-256 hash** is stored, in a table walled off from the
  tenant database role — the same identity-domain lockdown as SSO secrets.

For the design rationale, see
[ADR-0014](https://github.com/achref-soua/helio/blob/main/docs/adr/0014-scim-provisioning.md).

---
title: Rate limits & abuse protection
description: Where Helio throttles callers — shared budgets on the API gateway and ingestion, per-replica budgets on the dashboard's public endpoints, and brute-force damping on auth.
---

Helio rate-limits every surface an anonymous or semi-trusted caller can
reach. Throttled requests answer **429** with `Retry-After`,
`RateLimit-Limit`, and `RateLimit-Remaining` headers.

## Shared budgets (Redis)

The API gateway and the ingestion service count requests in Redis, so every
replica draws from the same budget:

| Surface              | Keyed by                 | Default budget | Tune with                        |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------- |
| REST gateway (`/v1`) | API key (fallback: IP)   | 100 / 60 s     | `RATE_LIMIT_MAX/WINDOW_S`        |
| Event ingestion      | Write key (fallback: IP) | 600 / 60 s     | `INGEST_RATE_LIMIT_MAX/WINDOW_S` |

## Dashboard public endpoints (per replica)

The dashboard's public, unauthenticated endpoints use an in-process fixed
window keyed by client IP (plus the write key where one applies, so tenants
behind one IP never share a budget). Budgets are per replica: scaling the
web deployment to N replicas multiplies the effective ceiling by N, which is
fine for abuse damping.

| Surface                            | Budget per IP / minute |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Widget config (`/api/widgets`)     | 120 (per IP + key)     |
| In-app message poll (`/api/inapp`) | 240 read / 60 write    |
| Hosted form submissions            | 30                     |
| Public meeting booking             | 30                     |
| SCIM provisioning (`/scim/v2`)     | 240                    |

Set `PUBLIC_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED=false` to disable these during load tests.

The **unsubscribe endpoints are deliberately exempt**: they are
HMAC-token-authed (unguessable, and an invalid token does no database work),
and one-click unsubscribe must always land — throttling it would be a
compliance bug, not a protection.

## Auth brute-force damping

Better-Auth's limiter is active in production with tight budgets on the
credential endpoints (per IP, per replica):

| Endpoint                                    | Budget     |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `/sign-in/email`, `/sign-up/email`          | 10 / 60 s  |
| `/forget-password`                          | 5 / 300 s  |
| Two-factor verification (TOTP, backup code) | 10 / 60 s  |
| Everything else under `/api/auth`           | 120 / 60 s |

## Trusting the client IP

All IP-keyed budgets read the first hop of `X-Forwarded-For`. That header is
only meaningful when a fronting proxy **overwrites** it — terminate TLS at a
proxy or ingress that does (the bundled Compose and Helm setups assume
this), and never expose the Node services directly to the internet.

# Pull-request and trunk CI — the automated form of `task verify`. Until now
# the only gate was running that locally, which is how a red e2e suite and a
# journey double-send reached a release. This runs on every PR into develop/
# main and on every push to them, so regressions are caught before merge.
#
# The `verify` and `python` jobs mirror `task verify` (format, lint, typecheck,
# TS tests, then the Python checks). The `e2e` job runs the Playwright suite
# against a real core stack (Postgres + Redis + Mailpit) — it used to be out of
# CI entirely, which is exactly how a red e2e suite reached a release.
#
# e2e runs on every PR and push and is a hard gate: a red shard fails the run.
# It was informational while four specs failed under the 2-core shard for
# environment/correctness reasons (a dev-only env flag the CI app never read, a
# test reading a button label instead of the booking link); those are fixed and
# the suite has been green with zero retries across consecutive runs. To make a
# red shard also block the merge, add the `e2e (1..4)` contexts to the develop/
# main required-status-checks ruleset. Locally it stays `task verify:e2e`.
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [develop, main]
  push:
    branches: [develop, main]

# A newer push to the same ref cancels the in-flight run.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Format
        run: pnpm format:check
      - name: Lint
        run: pnpm lint
      - name: Typecheck
        run: pnpm typecheck
      # Includes the Testcontainers integration tests; the runner's Docker
      # daemon backs them. The Temporal tests use the in-process time-skipping
      # environment, so no external services are needed.
      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test

  python:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
      # The intelligence RLS data-isolation tests build their schema by shelling
      # out to `pnpm --filter @helio/db exec prisma migrate deploy` against a
      # Testcontainers Postgres, so this job needs node + pnpm too.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Intelligence — lint, types, tests
        working-directory: apps/intelligence
        run: uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy && uv run pytest
      - name: Python SDK — lint, types, tests
        working-directory: packages/sdk-py
        run: uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy && uv run pytest

  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Shard the serial suite across parallel runners. The single-worker run took
    # ~20 min, and the contention made heavy /settings dialogs flake; sharding
    # cuts wall-clock and per-runner load. Each shard brings up its own stack and
    # truncates its own DB in global setup, so they're fully isolated.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    env:
      # Admin owns DDL; the app connects as the RLS-bound helio_app role the
      # migration creates (dev-default password). These match .env.example, which
      # the compose stack below uses, so the app and the datastores agree.
      DATABASE_ADMIN_URL: postgresql://helio:helio_dev_password@localhost:5432/helio
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://helio_app:helio_app@localhost:5432/helio
      MAILPIT_UI_PORT: '8025'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # Bring the core stack up via the project's OWN compose so the containers
      # are named exactly as locally (helio-postgres-1, …): several specs assert
      # DB state with `docker exec helio-postgres-1 psql`, which GitHub Actions
      # `services:` can't satisfy. Mirrors `task verify:e2e` (which needs `task up`).
      - name: Start the core stack (Postgres + Redis + Mailpit)
        run: docker compose --env-file .env.example -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml --profile core up -d --wait
      # Ephemeral per-run secrets — nothing sensitive lives in the workflow.
      # Lengths satisfy the env schema (auth >= 32, unsubscribe >= 24); the
      # base64 key lets the credential-vault specs exercise their real path.
      - name: Generate ephemeral e2e secrets
        run: |
          {
            echo "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
            echo "UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
            echo "HELIO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Apply the database schema
        run: pnpm --filter @helio/db exec prisma migrate deploy
      - name: Build the web app
        # next start serves whatever build is on disk, so build current code.
        # env.ts validates the runtime schema at build time (it's imported when
        # collecting page data), so provide build-time placeholders — the real
        # values are read at runtime by next start. Build directly via pnpm (db
        # first, then web; ui/core are transpiled from source) rather than turbo,
        # mirroring infra/docker/web.Dockerfile so the build env is unfiltered.
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @helio/db build
          BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=[REDACTED] \
          DATABASE_URL=postgresql://build:build@localhost:5432/build \
          DATABASE_ADMIN_URL=postgresql://build:build@localhost:5432/build \
          UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET=[REDACTED] \
            pnpm --filter @helio/web build
      - name: Install the Playwright browser
        run: pnpm --filter @helio/web exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Run e2e shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4 (Playwright boots the app on :3100)
        run: cd apps/web && CI=1 pnpm test:e2e --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4
      - name: Upload the Playwright report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: apps/web/test-results
          retention-days: 7

{
  "name": "@helio/sdk-js",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "description": "Helio JS/TS SDK: browser event tracking (track/identify/page) and a typed REST client for the public API gateway.",
  "license": "AGPL-3.0-only",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    ".": "./src/index.ts",
    "./rest": "./src/rest.ts"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "eslint .",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "vitest run --coverage",
    "generate": "openapi-typescript ../../apps/api/openapi.json -o src/openapi.d.ts"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@helio/config": "workspace:*",
    "@types/node": "^25.9.2",
    "@vitest/coverage-v8": "^4.1.8",
    "eslint": "^10.4.1",
    "jsdom": "^28.0.0",
    "openapi-typescript": "^7.13.0",
    "typescript": "^6.0.3",
    "vitest": "^4.1.8"
  }
}

{
  "name": "@helio/api",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "description": "Helio public REST gateway — OpenAPI 3.1, problem+json errors, rate limiting, idempotency.",
  "license": "AGPL-3.0-only",
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "tsx watch src/server.ts",
    "lint": "eslint .",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "vitest run --coverage",
    "openapi": "tsx src/scripts/write-openapi.ts",
    "build": "esbuild src/server.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --external:pg-native --banner:js=\"import { createRequire } from 'node:module'; const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);\" --outfile=dist/server.mjs"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@helio/core": "workspace:*",
    "@helio/db": "workspace:*",
    "@hono/node-server": "^2.0.4",
    "@hono/zod-openapi": "^1.4.0",
    "@opentelemetry/api": "^1.9.1",
    "@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node": "^0.76.0",
    "@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http": "^0.218.0",
    "@opentelemetry/sdk-node": "^0.218.0",
    "hono": "^4.12.25",
    "ioredis": "^5.11.1",
    "pino": "^10.3.1",
    "pino-http": "^11.0.0",
    "prom-client": "^15.1.3",
    "zod": "^4.4.3"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@helio/config": "workspace:*",
    "@testcontainers/postgresql": "^12.0.1",
    "@types/ioredis-mock": "^8.2.7",
    "@types/node": "^25.9.2",
    "@vitest/coverage-v8": "^4.1.8",
    "esbuild": "^0.28.0",
    "eslint": "^10.4.1",
    "ioredis-mock": "^8.13.1",
    "tsx": "^4.22.4",
    "typescript": "^6.0.3",
    "vitest": "^4.1.8"
  }
}

[project]
name = "helio-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
description = "Helio's Python SDK: a typed client for the public REST API."
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "httpx>=0.27",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.3",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0",
    "ruff>=0.7",
    "mypy>=1.13",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/helio_sdk"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "C4"]

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
files = ["src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--cov=helio_sdk --cov-report=term --cov-fail-under=80"
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src"]

# helio-sdk (Python)

Helio's Python SDK — a typed client for the public REST API. Built on
[`httpx`](https://www.python-httpx.org/), managed with [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

## Install

```bash
uv add helio-sdk   # or: pip install helio-sdk
```

## Usage

```python
from helio_sdk import HelioApiError, HelioClient

with HelioClient(
    api_key="[REDACTED]",  # Settings → API keys; server-side only
    base_url="https://api.your-helio.example",
) as helio:
    contact = helio.create_contact(
        workspace_id="ws_...",
        email="jane@example.com",
        first_name="Jane",
        idempotency_key="...",
    )

    vips = helio.create_list(workspace_id="ws_...", name="VIPs")
    helio.add_list_members(vips["id"], [contact["id"]])

    # Cursor pagination.
    cursor: str | None = None
    while True:
        page = helio.list_contacts(workspace_id="ws_...", cursor=cursor)
        for c in page["data"]:
            print(c["email"])
        cursor = page["nextCursor"]
        if cursor is None:
            break

    try:
        helio.get_contact("contact_missing")
    except HelioApiError as error:
        print(error.status, error.type, error.detail)
```

Resources: `list_workspaces` / `create_workspace`; `list_contacts` /
`create_contact` / `get_contact` / `update_contact` / `delete_contact`;
`list_lists` / `create_list` / `get_list` / `delete_list` /
`add_list_members` / `remove_list_member`.

## Notes

- The API key grants full organization access — keep it **server-side**.
- Responses are typed `TypedDict`s matching the API's JSON (camelCase keys).
- `update_contact(..., first_name=None)` clears a field; omitting the
  argument leaves it unchanged.
- Every non-2xx response raises `HelioApiError` carrying the RFC 9457
  problem document (`status`, `type`, `title`, `detail`).
